etymologies.etymologyHTML: From mid 17th century, equivalent to re- +‎ mind (“to remember”). Probably suggested by obsolete rememorate with the same sense. Displaced Old English myndgian.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause one to experience a memory (of someone or something); to bring to the notice or consideration (of a person).

quote.citation: 1849, Currer Bell [pseudonym; Charlotte Brontë], chapter 3, in Shirley. A Tale. […], volume (please specify |volume=I to III), London: Smith, Elder and Co., […], →OCLC:
quote.text: I am aware, reader, and you need not remind me, that it is a dreadful thing for a parson to be warlike.

quote.citation: 1915, Joseph Conrad, “Author's Note”, in Victory: An Island Tale:
quote.text: His eyes were green and every cat I see to this day reminds me of the exact contour of his face.

definitions.definition: (colloquial or nonstandard) An act of reminding; a reminder.

quote.citation: 2014 March 30, “EPS canine units track down 7 suspects in 6 hours”, in CBC News‎[1], archived from the original on 2016-01-15:
quote.text: Even with successful nights like that, Garth said the death of police dog Quanto in October is never forgotten, but instead serves as a remind that any call could be dangerous.

quote.citation: 2023 April 19, Anna Nora Tassetti et al., “The BlueBio project's database: web-mapping cooperation to create value for the Blue Bioeconomy”, in Scientific Data, volume 10, London: Nature Portfolio, →DOI, →ISSN, →OCLC:
quote.text: Surveys consisted of circulating a questionnaire - in .xls file with predefined fields to fill - amongst information producers (i.e., project coordinators, national research funding agencies involved in BlueBio projects); several reminds were sent to increase the response rate.
